Two NEW guards created: test:mesh-grid (first automated check of any kind to reach mesh-export/, a premium surface that had none) and 16 new assertions in test:gmf. The mesh-export work was guard-first - the guard was written BEFORE the VDB fix, failed on both translation rows with the exact diagnosis, then passed after and found one row instead of two, independently confirming the de-duplication. The most severe finding of the run: pre-2026-04-25 scene files carry flat-shaped savedCameras with no migration, and loading one then opening the Camera Manager UNMOUNTED THE ENTIRE REACT ROOT - white screen, frames frozen, unsaved work lost. The verifier closed the gap the original investigation left by driving the REAL load path with a real filechooser and the real 2026-04-15 file from disk, plus a control run with a modern row proving the shape was responsible. It also established there is NO ErrorBoundary anywhere in the codebase, which is why any render throw is fatal. Fixed and re-verified against the same rows. Both verifiers corrected their claims materially: the mesh... no, the graph verifier found MANDELBOX_PIPELINE has zero importers (dead code, not a shipped preset) so the claimed symptom does not occur - then constructed a worse real one - and discovered a THIRD bug neither claim mentioned: autoCompile is never initialized and setAutoCompile never implemented, so the Auto checkbox throws a TypeError when clicked and branch A of setGraph is dead code. g10 fixed an undo bug falsification-first. Notable: g10 investigated whether its own guard citation was another wrong-guard case, falsified it, found the citation defensible, and declined to manufacture a finding.

Four subsystems closed in one cycle by three auditors (the two 1-file toys were batched into one agent), leaving only p01-palette-suite. 20 Tier A commits, ZERO Tier V - the second cycle of the run where every finding was either self-guarding or an owner call, so the verifier step was skipped legitimately rather than cut. THE CYCLE WAS NOT CLOSED OUT WHEN THE AUDITORS FINISHED: the orchestrator turn ended at 23:29Z with all 20 commits on the branch but no results files, no worklist update, no journal entry and no dashboard - a 6h45m gap until the owner asked at 06:13Z. Nothing was lost from the tree, but the a03-tutorial auditor RETURN VALUE was lost, and its record in results/ is reconstructed from commit messages. Its three Tier A findings survive intact because the commit bodies carry their own verification inline; any Tier B or V it returned is gone. The generalisable fix is that the cycle-close bookkeeping should not depend on the orchestrator surviving to the end of a long turn - write results/<id>.json as each auditor returns, not in a batch at the end. THE GUARD STORY IS THE CYCLE. Three independent falsifications converged on the same structural hole. smoke:fluid-brush was RED AT BASELINE on a clean tree and had been written off in fluid-toy README as Chromium GPU flake - the real cause is that fluid-toy boots as a pure fractal explorer (paused defaults true, composite shows julia only), so the dye buffer the brush writes is never composited and any naive pixel assertion measures nothing. Repaired, then re-falsified twice, and its threshold was found too loose to catch the very regression it exists for (a one-splat break scored 5.2 against a threshold of 5 and PASSED) so it was recalibrated to 40 with the measurement recorded. Separately smoke:undo - the ONLY guard whose entry graph reaches app-gmt/tutorial/** - was falsified by inverting the bool trigger comparator and stayed fully green 20/20, a 13th instance of the blind-guard class. And check:rule-guards, the mechanical checker meant to catch exactly that, was falsified NEGATIVELY in both directions: it matches guards against a rule whole paths: set (so per-row miscitation is invisible in a five-app rule) and it resolves a chained npm script by its first command only (which made a correct new citation report a FALSE issue). The a03 and gx01 auditors reached that same conclusion from opposite ends of the tree without seeing each other work. Also notable: the gx01 auditor caught and corrected its OWN error mid-cycle - its first citation of test:palette pushed the shared check:rule-guards baseline from 4 issues to 5, and it re-cited the test module directly and re-verified the baseline back at 4 rather than leaving it. smoke:liquify measured at ~23% false-red over 13 clean runs and was deliberately NOT falsified, because a guard that noisy cannot distinguish a regression from itself - that is Tier B with a proven-template fix. smoke:gx-fractal-glitch, the only ADR-0065/0066 coverage in the repo, could not be baselined at all: two attempts killed by Vite full-reloads from concurrent auditors editing tracked source, which is a real cost of the 3-agent shared-tree model and is now on record. One process defect: parallel auditors share one working tree and the a03 auditor staged with a broad add, sweeping 54 lines of the gx01 auditor docs/modules/gradient-explorer/app.md work into commit 50d18282. No content lost, history not rewritten, but that finding is mis-attributed in the log and PROTOCOL.md should require explicit-path staging. Both auditors declined work they could have done and said why: neither touched CLAUDE.md despite proving 2 of the 5 sibling-app doc paths it names do not exist (steering config is the owner call), neither rewrote a flaky guard unattended, and the toy auditor left frozen audit-provenance frontmatter alone rather than half-updating it.

TWO MORE GUARDS THAT CANNOT FAIL, which is now the defining theme of this run. (1) The oklab drift pin in test-palette-stopops.mts compares a function against itself - oklab.ts re-exports lerpOklab from utils/colorUtils, so both sides of a 448-sample loop are the same function object. Measured: a 0.024% perturbation of rgbToOklab M-matrix leaves the whole 16-link chain green. (2) p01b broke GradientStrip so EVERY gradient strip in the suite renders blank; test:palette exit 0, typecheck exit 0. Neither is a fault in test:palette, which is healthy for what it covers - the gap is that the name implies coverage the chain does not have. The palette component layer, 30 files and 6257 lines including the PickerWall index math and the FavientsPanel drop logic, has ZERO automated coverage. A THIRD NUL-BYTE FILE. debug/test-palette-importformats.mts held a raw 0x00, so ripgrep classified it binary and skipped it - the only guard covering palette/core/importFormats.ts was invisible to every grep-based pass including all of run 1. Found independently by two auditors; fixed by escaping the bytes with the runtime string unchanged. The tree-wide NUL scan is now clean. THE STAGING RULE ADDED THIS MORNING WAS BREACHED THE SAME DAY, and the diagnosis is the valuable part. Two auditors did exactly as instructed - git add on one explicit path, git status --porcelain checked immediately before committing - and p01b ChannelGraphEditor change still landed inside p01a commit a2f1ec49. Cause: parallel auditors share one working tree and therefore one git INDEX, and add+commit is not atomic across processes, so no discipline at the add step can close it. p01a diagnosed it mid-run and switched to the pathspec form, git commit -F <msg> -- <paths>, which commits only the named paths whatever else is in the index; p01b independently adopted a post-commit git log -1 --name-only check. Both are now in PROTOCOL.md, with one git worktree per auditor named as the clean structural answer. This is the second protocol amendment in a day derived from an actual failure rather than from theory. Auditors again declined work and said why: none created .claude/rules/palette.md despite all three finding the gap and all three drafting a section for it, because three concurrent writers to one new file is exactly the collision the run keeps hitting. The merged draft sits in their notes for the orchestrator to assemble. None touched CLAUDE.md, whose palette path is wrong - steering config, owner call, and that is now the second subsystem to confirm it independently. p01a also answered both palette seam questions cycle 11 handed forward, including the useful negative that sampleGeometry is NOT drifting toward statefulness so the Gradient Explorer byte-identical contract is safe today.

THE GUARD SWEEP, COMPLETE. Run serially - one agent at a time on a quiet tree - because parallel agents killed a browser smoke twice in cycle 12. All 76 worklist guards falsified; the other 9 of package.json's original 85 had already been falsified during the cycle-11/12 subsystem audits, so every guard the repo shipped has now been broken deliberately and watched. 44 of 76 were defective - just under 60%. The dominant failure mode was not in the protocol at the start and was added to it mid-sweep as a fifth: GREEN BECAUSE THE INPUT VANISHED. test:frag printed 0 passed 0 failed exit 0 with its ~580-file corpus missing; test:shader all-passed with 87% of its formula matrix absent; smoke:gx-fractal-glitch printed its full glitch-free banner on a COMPLETELY BLANK render; test:frag:integration:discover is deliberately permanently red so a vanished corpus INVERTED it to green. Its close cousin, named in batch 7: a negative assertion must prove its subject exists first. The single most load-bearing find was smoke:engine-gmt - cited as proof by 13 applied findings and unable to fail on a shader with a hard GLSL syntax error, because hasCompiledShader is an optimistic latch set when a compile is ISSUED and the broken shader rendered empty frames FASTER than a working one. The last batch broke the pattern: smoke:all had been permanently RED, dying at member 28 of 42 because four members pointed at vite stock port 5173 while this repo pins 3400 - so FOURTEEN members never ran, including smoke:interact which CLAUDE.md lists as an automated check. Behind that port sat a harness reading an absolute path into the dev/ tree deleted six weeks earlier. And smoke:with-server could not execute a line of its job on Windows, a breakage so old that ADR-0073 had written it down as a platform fact to route around. Neither was ever falsely green; both were loudly red, which is exactly why they survived. check:rule-guards went from 4 miscitations to ZERO, and was itself repaired TWICE - blind to npm-run composites (batch 7), then to bare-tsx chains (batch 9b), seeing 1 of smoke:all's 42 members. Three rules were written for subsystems that had none - deep-zoom.md, interaction-session.md, gmt-shader-chunks.md - each because a healthy guard had nowhere to be cited from. Four npm scripts were created for harnesses reachable only through a 42-member chain, which is why two of them had rotted unnoticed.
